messages:
mira: quick brain dump on 'tail-steering' as a mitigator for p95 regressions during canaries. idea: instead of moving X% of all traffic away, route only tail-ish requests (high-cost/longest) to fallback to protect latency SLOs.
hank: interesting. how do we identify tail requests without adding client latency?
mira: two options: 1) estimator at admission based on request features (prompt length, model, expected tokens), 2) lightweight fast-path probe: sample incoming requests and build a small model that predicts cost. both are opt-in per-route.
olivia: estimator seems simplest. also good for large models where token count correlates strongly with latency. but estimator must be deterministic and auditable.
kevin: router needs a stable hash so we can slowly shift tail routing. we can't use full request body for routing in Private. maybe use length buckets + model type + hashed tenant id.
mira: agreed. config snippet idea: ```yaml
rollout_id: tail_canary_1
enabled: true
steering_mode: tail_sample
tail_selector:
  method: estimator
  threshold_percentile: 95
  min_sample_rate: 0.5
```
hank: what about fairness? steering tails could bias the user experience for heavy users. product will want transparency.
mira: surface in console: "Tail-steering active: X% of tail requests routed to fallback" and include appeal + audit logs. tenants can opt out or set max_steered_pct.
kevin: failure modes? if estimator misclassifies, we might steer too many requests. add confidence and kill-switch. Also blend with adjudicator: only apply tail-steering after soft-eviction confidence > 0.7.
olivia: also consider a dual-probe: run fallback for a fraction of tail requests to compare quality. that prevents silent quality regressions.
security: note: any estimator using request metadata must avoid leaking PII. keep selectors based on non-sensitive fields (token_count, model, route).
mira: good. telemetry: add metrics: tail_steered.count, tail_estimator.confidence, tail_quality.delta (score of fallback vs variant).
hank: router change: need an API to accept a steering policy with fields {selector, max_steer_pct, ttl, confidence_floor}. must be atomically applied to avoid partial state.
kevin: implementation: we can implement estimator as a tiny lib in router runtime with a pluggable model. default is rules-based: tokens > 400 -> tail. advanced: a small regression model from telemetry. ship rules first.
olivia: console: show tail histogram + who was affected. allow tenant owners to download anonymized example samples used to define threshold.
kevin: interactions with rejoin: tail-steering should be independent of soft-eviction. you can soft-evict 40% and also tail-steer 10% of tails. Need clear priority: hard_block > soft_eviction > tail_steering > normal routing.
mira: agreed. add to RFC order of precedence.
hank: operationally, we must avoid steering storms: if many routes enable tail-steering, fallback capacity must scale. router should check global fallback budget before applying a policy.
mira: yes global circuit and budget checks. also allow adjudicator to include a 'steer_priority' so high-impact routes get precedence.
olivia: one more UX ask: provide a simulation mode where ops can run tail-steering against historical traces and see projected p95 impact.
mira: add dry-run support for tail policies.
deploy-bot: scheduled: tail_canary_1 started by @mira at 3055554400, default tail selector rules applied.
kevin: i'll add steering fields to the adjudicator action proto and a minimal router feature flag. will prototype rule-based estimator first.
security: add to checklist: ensure no raw payloads are used in estimator; all sample exports must be redacted.
mira: great. i'll add the tail-steering section to the RFC with config + precedence + telemetry + dry-run instructions. sync next week for PoC results.
